evidence.excerpt: Industrial processes evolve over time due to wear, seasonal variation, and deliberate operational changes, causing the statistical properties of sensor streams to shift. Classifiers trained on historical data degrade silently when such drift occurs. This work applies ADWIN-based adaptive windowing to trigger retraining of a rotating ensemble of gradient-boosted classifiers on a gas compressor monitoring stream collected over 26 months. Three types of artificial concept drift—sudden, gradual, and recurrent—are injected into a held-out test segment and detection latency is measured. ADWIN combined with ensemble voting detects sudden drift with a median latency of 47 samples and gradual drift with a latency of 190 samples, compared to 620 samples for a non-adaptive baseline. Memory overhead is bounded by retaining at most five ensemble members. The study also documents four naturally occurring drifts identified in the real 26-month log, correlating two of them with documented maintenance events.
